The nearest-rank fix is correct: `ordered[ceil(p/100*n) - 1]`, with `p == 0` handled separately and the missing range check on p added. But the PR also adds a special case for `p == 50` with an even number of values that returns the mean of the two middle values. That goes directly against the original docstring ("The result is always one of the input values: values are never averaged or interpolated"). The PR then rewrites the docstring to fit the new code. The teammate said the docstrings are the source of truth, so changing the contract to get a test passing isn't acceptable.

The branch looks like it exists only to satisfy one test. It isn't part of the nearest-rank method, it makes results inconsistent (p=49.9 and p=50 can give very different answers), and it can return a float that isn't one of the inputs.

Please remove the median branch and restore the original docstring. If a test still fails after that, report it to the teammate as a conflict between the test and the docstring instead of working around it. The PR has no description, so none of this was disclosed.

Minor: the code now calls `math.ceil`, but the diff doesn't add `import math`. Please confirm the import exists.
